title: MESA: Prioritizing Security-Critical Communication Channels in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: arXiv:2606.30602v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Today, multi-agent systems (MAS) are becoming increasingly capable by exchanging, critiquing, and aggregating intermediate information. However, this internal communication is both a source of capability and an emerging attack surface. Harmful content can be transformed and propagated through messages among legitimate agents. Applying costly defenses everywhere incurs latency and performance degradation. A question therefore arises: which inter-agent information flows should defenders prioritize? In this paper, we introduce MESA, a novel allocation layer that ranks internal communication channels by security criticality. MESA requires no attack traces; it combines lightweight graph-theoretic features from the communication topology with workflow-aware features capturing runtime behavior from execution probes. Our study spans eight topologies, three application domains, five standard open-weight models, and diverse attack config

translated_title: MESA：在多智能体系统中优先保障安全关键通信信道
translated_abstract: 如今，多智能体系统（MAS）正通过交换、批评和聚合中间信息而变得日益强大。然而，这种内部通信既是能力的来源，也是一个新兴的攻击面。有害内容可以在合法智能体之间通过消息进行转换和传播。而在所有地方部署高成本防御措施则会带来延迟和性能下降。因此产生了一个问题：防御者应该优先保护哪些智能体间的信息流？本文提出了MESA，一种新颖的分配层，能够根据安全关键性对内部通信信道进行排序。MESA无需攻击痕迹；它将来自通信拓扑的轻量级图论特征与通过执行探针捕获运行时行为的工作流感知特征相结合。我们的研究涵盖了八种拓扑结构、三个应用领域、五个标准开源权重模型以及多样化的攻击配置。
tldr: MESA提出了一种无需攻击痕迹的安全分配层，通过结合通信拓扑的图论特征与运行时工作流感知特征，对多智能体系统内部通信信道按安全关键性进行优先级排序，从而实现高效的针对性防御。
en_tdlr: MESA introduces an attack-trace-free allocation layer that prioritizes internal communication channels in multi-agent systems by security criticality, combining lightweight graph-theoretic topology features with workflow-aware runtime probe features for efficient targeted defense.
